title: Return the last item
prompt: `LastOr<T>(List<T> items, T fallback)` should return the last item of the list, or `fallback` when the list is empty. It must work for a list of any type. The starter always returns the fallback.
hints: At which position is the last item of a list with Count items?
Positions start at 0, so the last one is Count - 1. An empty list has no last item.
Return fallback when items.Count is 0. Otherwise return items[items.Count - 1].
checkLabels: The last of 4 and 9 must be 9.
An empty list of ints must give the fallback.
The last of "a" and "b" must be "b".
An empty list of strings must give the fallback.
A list with one item must give that item.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Returns the first item instead of the last.
Reads the last position of a list that has none.

feedback: Try a list of two items and an empty list. Check which position you read and what happens when Count is 0.
